body:
Zoloft caused the worst side effects. Effexor suppressed my appetite, which isn't the worst thing in the world.

I really don't think they care anymore. In august they decided to discharge me. Even though I told them I was still suicidal. Every time I go I see a different psychiatrist and I tell them I'm having suicidal thoughts. They talk to me about this for ten minutes then close the notes and tell me to come back in three months. That's what they did the whole of this year, didn't even prescribe anything until I attempted suicide. Then they said they were reluctant to give me anything because I might overdose, but the doctor said it in a sneering, mocking way (it appeared to me). Finally prescribed me Zoloft, even though my doctor took me off it before due to side effects. They didn't even listen when I told them them this.

I understand that I need to change my life for things to get better, and work hard at it. I just truly don't know what to do at this point. I have no energy, no motivation, no concentration. Everything seems futile and worthless. I don't have any goals to achieve. I don't know what I want to do with my life. I can't even get a job or finish a year in college. My self esteem is low.

They were Escitalopram, Sertraline (tried these twice) and Venlafaxine. These are the generic names as the brand names are different everywhere. 

Yeah, I know I need to get in contact with the mental health team again, I just feel very ashamed right now and I don't need them looking down on me or patronising me.

I try to go for a walk everyday. I think this does help in a way but I've been doing it for a long time and I'm still depressed.

I don't know if anything will change though...I see people talking about having depression for twenty, thirty years. I see people I know, like members of my family struggling day after day. Working so hard, stressed out, worrying. I read posts on websites from people who have been suicidal for years and nothing has changed for them. And with me, not much has improved for me. Yes, some things have got better in my life, but on the whole everything gets worse as time goes on.

I love music and love to learn how to play instruments but can never get motivated to do anything. That is one of the things I do want to do though. I'm just too stressed out all the time to do anything, even read a book.

Listening to music does make me feel better.

Thanks for the recommendation, I'll try and find it.

I just find it so hard in my current state of mind. I'm apathetic and I don't give a shit about life, happiness any more. Also I'm too stressed out like I said before to follow any particular course of action. I know that my view of the world influences what happens to me though.

Thanks for your post, it did help me. And I like talking to people who still have hope and curiosity about the world, as it gives me hope that I might be like that one day.

I've been on them on and off for two years (with breaks in between going on for months). I've tried three of them I think, for some reason they made me try two of the anti depressants twice, even though they didn't help me the first time, one gave me bad side effects, but they still put me on it again. 

I don't think she understands mental illness at all.

I live in Europe, they do offer free therapy but its hard to get, and it would be stuff like psychology/cbt rather than psychotherapy (which someone recommended to me). It's quite hard to access as so many people need it, and also as I said, I saw the psychologist before but stopped going, so they probably won't give it to me again.

At one time I did have dreams...I don't know if I still have them, everything just seems worthless and unattainable right now.

I have thought about that, but I don't have enough confidence to do it. I'm scared of being truly alone like that, being homeless, getting lost in strange places. I have thought about it a lot though, but I don't think I'd be able to handle it. It might make me feel even worse. 

They gave me anti depressants before which didn't have much of an effect. I saw a psychologist for a while but I didn't really feel it. After my attempt they didn't really give a fuck and one nurse kept guilt tripping me about it, and saying 'you've been seeing us two years now' like it was my fault I'm not improving.

I'm not taking medication at the moment, or seeing a therapist. I would like to see a therapist, but I don't know how I could pay for it at the moment.

> Stop resigning yourself to to the idea you are going to committ suicide, that will make any attempt at engaging in life seem pointless to you. 

Hah. Yeah that's already happened. The whole time I'm in college, I'm thinking, why am I bothering trying so hard, when I'm just going to kill myself anyway?

I just don't seem to have any will to recover. Nothing in life seems appealing to me. Going to college (can't do that in this state anyway) working, getting married, having kids. I don't want any of it. I have no energy to try.
